ground_truth: The `payWithERC20` function is public and allows the caller to specify the `fromAddress`. An attacker can use this to drain the entire approved token balance from any user who has granted an allowance to the `BlueprintV5` contract.

The function to create agent deployment requests hardcodes a request index to `0`. If a user creates two requests for the same project in the same block, the second request will overwrite the first, causing the user to lose the fee for the initial request.

Functions using EIP-712 signatures for gasless transactions fail to include all critical parameters in the signed message. An attacker can replay a valid signature with malicious parameters, forcing the user into an unwanted action or causing a loss of funds.

The `updateWorkerDeploymentConfigWithSig` function lacks replay protection like a nonce. An attacker can capture a valid signature and replay it multiple times to drain a user's approved token allowance by repeatedly triggering the fee payment.

The `setWorkerPublicKey` function is public, allowing anyone to register as a worker. A malicious worker can then be selected by a user, allowing the worker to intercept encrypted data and refuse to complete the deployment, causing the user to lose their fee.

There is no timeout or cancellation mechanism for a deployment request once a worker has picked it up. A malicious or offline worker can leave a project permanently stalled, as no new requests can be made.

A whitelist for creating agents is easily bypassed. While one function (`createAgentWithWhitelistUsers`) enforces a whitelist, another public function (`createAgentWithNFT`) allows anyone with a specific NFT to create an agent with no such check.
